text:
Marathon Petroleum stock gained 2.3% today as oil prices approached $100 per barrel amid escalating U.S.-Iran tensions in the Middle East. The geopolitical flare-up has stoked concerns about potential supply disruptions, and refineries are running at 98% capacity — near maximum — which means higher crude costs feed more directly into refinery margins and profits. The stock is up nearly 10% over the past two weeks as this crisis has unfolded.

Refinery operators like Marathon benefit when crude oil prices rise in a supply-constrained environment because they can still sell gasoline and diesel at premium prices. With refineries already running flat-out and crude becoming scarcer and pricier due to Middle East risk, the margin between what they pay for oil and what they get for refined products widens — a straightforward tailwind for the business.
